concerns.text: T027 mandates generating a Negative Binomial null model 'from theoretical priors only' and explicitly forbids using pre-aggregation/permutation for the NB model. This contradicts FR-003 and Plan.md which require the NB model to be 'fitted to the observed data' (using robust stats). The task deliverable (theoretical-only model) falls short of the FR requirement (data-fitted model), constituting a semantic weakening of the statistical rigor constraint.

Tasks T014e-override, T060, and T070 mandate a 'Fail Loud' strategy that aborts the pipeline if real data is missing. This directly violates the Plan.md's explicit 'Synthetic Data Fallback' contingency strategy and the Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires the pipeline to run on a fresh runner even if external data is unavailable. The tasks silently relax the requirement for a reproducible CI pipeline by introducing a hard failure condition not present in the spec/plan.

FR-005 requires a sensitivity analysis sweeping thresholds over a resolved set {0.01%, [deferred], [deferred]}. T039a-resolve defines the set as '{%, 0.05%, 0.1%}' leaving a literal '%' placeholder, and T039d compares against '([deferred], [deferred], [deferred])'. This fails to concretely resolve the acceptance criteria into a testable set, violating the requirement for a defined sensitivity sweep and leaving the SC-003 measurement undefined.

FR-003 and FR-009 require 10,000 iterations with chunked processing to stay under 7GB RAM. T029 defines chunking as '10 batches of [deferred] iterations'. Without resolving the batch size (e.g., 1000), the memory constraint (7GB) is untestable and the iteration count (10,000) is unverifiable in the task definition, violating the requirement for a deterministic, constrained execution.

T063 mandates a deterministic sampling strategy to extract 'the first 10,000 jurisdictions' if the dataset exceeds 50,000. The Spec's Assumption about data availability only permits exclusion of missing variables, not arbitrary scope reduction via sampling unless 'necessary' for size. This task introduces a scope reduction (sampling) not explicitly authorized by the spec, risking violation of the 'Single Source of Truth' principle if the sample is not representative of the full population required for the discrepancy analysis.
